verdict_summary: Roughly a fifth of this list is a real missing principle; the rest is defect backlog, duplicate coverage, or process machinery a one-person pre-launch team cannot pay for. Three structural errors run through it: (1) about 21 findings prescribe a CI job, but origin/main is 1,604 commits and 66 days behind local main and the GitHub repo contains exactly one workflow file, so none of that CI has ever executed and every one of those rules would be law about a machine that does not exist; (2) at least nine findings are the estate's own already-pinned silent-no-op rule wearing new domain hats, and one of them (api-contracts-03) restates that rule almost verbatim while filing it as missing; (3) two agent CRITICALs were migration-file truths presented as live truths, which the orchestrator caught, and that error class is worth more than either finding. The failure mode of adopting this wholesale is precise and already measured in the owner's own audits: the estate has 164 hooks and 410,091 words in _design-system alone, the owner's own CLAUDE.md admits he does not re-read LOCKFILE before a small edit, and one 7-gate family was skip-flagged 72 times in 6 days. Adding 264 rules to a corpus nobody re-reads is a write-only operation; adding the gates to enforce them converts the skip flag into the normal workflow. The genuinely valuable output of this run is not the rule list, it is five measured facts: CI has never run, the remote is 66 days stale, the shipped browse pages sit at 4.4% and 0.0% imagery against a 33% floor, health data is stored with no consent record, and the ToS promises two things the code does not do.

merge.merged_principle: THE SILENT NO-OP RULE APPLIES TO THE MACHINERY, NOT ONLY TO PRODUCT FILTERS. The project's pinned rule already says: prove behavior, not existence; a filter must DISCRIMINATE, not merely render or return 200. Extend that same proof obligation, unchanged in wording, to every other thing in this estate that can look wired and do nothing: a consent or preference toggle must have a proven reader on a real send path; a verification endpoint that returns verified:true must persist the fact in the same request (and the column it writes must exist in the live schema); a table that records a penalty must have a reader that applies the consequence; a cron-health check must distinguish 'ran and failed' from 'never ran'; a gate, lint script or npm check must be proven to fire on a crafted failing input, not merely to exist in package.json; a CI job that can skip its whole body and still report green is a placebo; and every Terms of Service promise about verification, enforcement or consequence needs one end-to-end test that exercises it. One rule, one existing name, one new sentence about scope.

NOTHING MAY BE PRESCRIBED INTO CI UNTIL CI EXISTS ON THE REMOTE DEFAULT BRANCH. Verified this session: origin/main is at 4dd8bc15f (2026-05-21), local main is 1,604 commits ahead, and the GitHub repo's .github/workflows contains exactly one file (cron-jobs.yml); gh run list --workflow=quality.yml returns 404, not found on the default branch, and the five most recent runs of the one deployed workflow all failed in 5 to 7 seconds. Sixteen findings here propose a new CI job (a11y lint, axe target-size, Lighthouse budgets, npm audit ratchet, gitleaks, select(*) ratchet, i18n key parity, jscpd, diff-scoped lint). Every one of them is downstream of a single prerequisite, and adopting them as law before that prerequisite is met writes sixteen false guarantees into the doctrine. The merged principle: any doc sentence claiming a CI guarantee must name the workflow file AND its last green run on the remote default branch, and a health check must assert that the local workflow set equals the remote workflow set. Fix the prerequisite (push, add the missing secrets, confirm one green run), then reconsider the sixteen, most of which will still not be worth their maintenance at 28 salons.

THE MIGRATIONS FOLDER IS A HISTORY, NOT A DESCRIPTION OF THE DATABASE, AND THE DIVERGENCE IS THE RISK. Two independent agents in this run reported a CRITICAL that was a migration-file truth presented as a live truth (a permissive reviews UPDATE policy that does not exist live, and hash-fabricated amenity booleans that are false for all 20 active salons). Every claim about current schema, policy or data is made against the live database; the migration folder is evidence only about what a REPLAY would produce. Both questions are legitimate and they are different: 'is this true now' and 'would a restore make this true'. Every audit states which one it answered. The corollary is the actual danger and it subsumes the restore-drill finding: a replay-only landmine is invisible to every check this estate runs, because nothing ever replays the folder onto a clean database. One real restore drill closes both halves at once, so it outranks all four of the RLS-policy-hygiene findings it absorbs.

EVERY MEASURED DESIGN FLOOR IS ENFORCED AGAINST MOCKUPS AND NEVER AGAINST THE SHIPPED PAGE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE PROBLEM. Measured live this session at 390x844: /de home is 4.4% imagery against a 33% floor with 7 distinct font sizes against a ceiling of 4 and 42.1% of text at weight >= 600 against a 30% ceiling; /de/basel is 0.0% imagery, zero images of any kind on a 9,325px page, while 20 of 28 salons have a usable cover_photo_url in the database. Meanwhile mockup-floors-gate.py's entire check is the regex `floors:\s*\S.{20,}`, that is, the presence of twenty characters after the word 'floors:'. The merged rule replaces four separate proposals (measure the gate instead of grepping for a comment, add a Floors row to SENIOR_SCORECARD, extend the floors to desktop and tablet, reconcile the documented fallback with the shipped component): run check-geometry.mjs --floors-only against the SHIPPED routes on real data as the acceptance condition, at every viewport the estate claims to support, and treat a mockup-only pass as no evidence. Nothing else on this list changes what a customer sees as directly.

RESEARCH IS NOT LAW, AND THIS ESTATE IS PRODUCING RESEARCH FASTER THAN IT FREEZES DECISIONS. Eight findings across six domains say the same thing: _backend-system/ contains 15 research files and 8 audit files, its own README promises LAW.md, RATIONALE.md, AUDIT.md and QUESTIONS.md at the root, and none of those four exist. This is ONE work item (transcribe the existing Decision-candidates tables into one LAW.md, dated, one row per axis) and not eight principles. But it must be adopted together with law-layer-roi-test, because it is the exact shape that finding warns about: writing a sixteenth research topic (privacy) into a folder that has never frozen the first fifteen makes the problem worse, not better. Rule: a topic is done at 'law frozen and backlinked', never at 'research written', and no new research topic starts until the previous one has a LAW.md row.

THE LAW LAYER GETS A BUDGET AND A DECAY PATH, NOT TEN NEW META-RULES. Ten separate governance findings all describe one condition: the estate grows law faster than it retires it, and the excess is discharged through skip flags rather than through decisions. Measured: 164 hooks (134 global, 30 project), 410,091 words in _design-system top-level markdown, LOCKFILE at 19,637 words which the project CLAUDE.md itself says nobody re-reads before a small edit, 13+ PreToolUse gates denying one at a time on a single mockup Write, one 7-gate family skip-flagged 72 times in 6 days, 8 gates sitting on disk unwired while the law text cites one of them (no-decorative-image-gate.py) as if it were live. The single merged rule: every new law names the counted incidents from the last 90 days it would have prevented, its per-session cost, and the existing law it replaces; total wired hooks are capped with one-in-one-out past the current count; any gate skip-flagged more than 10 times in a rolling 7 days is auto-flagged for re-scope or retirement; and any law sentence that names a hook file is reconciled against the settings files by the health check. Adopting the other nine as separate rows would be the failure this rule exists to prevent.

ANYTHING RENDERED ABOVE THE [locale] SEGMENT MUST BE LOCALE-INDEPENDENT BY CONSTRUCTION. Verified live on /en/basel: document.documentElement.lang is 'de' on the English page (app/layout.tsx:39 hardcodes it, above the locale tree), and the skip link still reads 'Zum Inhalt springen'. app/not-found.tsx, the second one, hardcodes German 404 copy with a literal em dash next to the properly i18n'd app/[locale]/not-found.tsx. The root viewport export in the same file disables pinch-zoom for all four languages. One file, one structural rule, four defects: the root layout may contain no locale-dependent string and no user-hostile global (lang, skip link, viewport scalability); anything that must live there reads the locale from the request. A one-line CI grep for hardcoded German and lang= in app/layout.tsx is the check, once CI exists.

THE DESIGN SYSTEM'S REACH STOPS AT THE REACT TREE, AND THREE LIVE SURFACES ARE OUTSIDE IT. The salon payout invoice (app/api/salon/invoices/[payoutId]/route.ts, a document partners print), the transactional email templates (lib/email-templates/*.ts, still rendering pre-B&W-pivot teal #38B2AC and coral #FF6B6B), and lib/email.ts:584 (gift-card codes in font-family:monospace, a retired font by name) all generate their own HTML strings and therefore obey no token, no font law and no contrast check. One rule covers all three: any surface that emits HTML/CSS outside the component tree imports its colors, fonts and numerals from one shared exported constants file mirroring the LOCKFILE table, and the drift checker's scan globs include it. This is worth more than most of the visual findings because these are the only Solen artifacts a partner keeps a copy of.

A REPORT STATES ITS NEGATIVE SPACE, ITS SAMPLE, AND ITS METHOD, OR IT IS A VIBE. Eight findings across two agents describe one discipline. Merged: every report that claims verification also names what was in scope and deliberately not checked; every claim derived from inspecting a set states how many of how many were inspected and how the sample was chosen ('12 of 357 route handlers across auth, booking and payments', never 'I checked the routes'); every number the assistant produced itself ships with the command that regenerates it and is rounded to the precision that method supports; hedges (should, presumably, likely, probably, I believe) are banned about anything runnable, readable or greppable, replaced by either the check or an explicit 'I did not check this'; and if the load-bearing claim of the turn could not be verified, that goes in the first line, above the work. This run is its own proof: three agents wrote 'every upload route trusts client file.type' having read four or five of them, and two wrote migration-file state as live state. Adopt this as ONE addition to REPORT_SYSTEM section 4, not as eight.

IF THE USER CAN GET BACK TO IT, IT LIVES IN THE URL OR IN STORAGE, NEVER ONLY IN MEMORY. Four findings describe one boundary: the booking wizard holds all step state in React context with no popstate guard, /inspo seeds only two of six filter dimensions from searchParams while /search seeds all of them, no page restores scroll position on back-navigation, and multi-step forms lose everything on refresh. The merged rule is the state-ownership half of fe-03 applied to navigation: anything that should be shareable, back-button-safe, or survive a refresh (a filter, an active step, a search query, a selected date, a scroll position) lives in the URL or in per-flow session storage, and a flow that cannot be reconstructed from its URL alone must intercept back and refresh with the same confirmation its explicit exit control already shows. One rule replaces four surface-specific ones and also absorbs ia-navigation-10 (a query param name carries one meaning app-wide).

bloat_risk: Concretely: 264 findings at roughly 90 words of paste-ready rule text each is about 24,000 new words, a 6% increase on the 410,091 words already in _design-system top-level markdown (measured this session with wc -w). That number understates the damage, because the binding constraint here is not disk, it is what gets re-read. The project CLAUDE.md says so in its own voice, as the stated reason its ten taste rules were duplicated inline: SOURCE.md and LOCKFILE hold the full system, but they are 80KB+ and I do not re-read them before a small edit, so I drift. Adding 264 rows to a corpus whose own author has documented that he cannot re-read it is a write-only operation, and this run has already added 896KB across 28 JSON files under _design-system/research/ before a single rule was adopted. The gate side is worse and is already measured. The estate has 164 wired hooks (134 global plus 30 project).
